sec.title: Tensor Computation Software
sec.p: There is an urgent need to explore and investigate tensor computation software packages in processing high-dimensional modern seismic data involving tensor decompositions, which is convenient for readers to develop and customize their own tensor-based seismic data analysis methods. With the flourishing development of tensor computation software, various feature-rich software packages have emerged as indispensable tools to drive applied research in tensor computation. Therefore, drawing inspiration from [1]’s work, it is necessary to conduct a review to select the most suitable software package for readers’ usage, with detailed summaries in Table A.1.

In Table A.1, we observed that Python, MATLAB, and C/C++ are the primary languages for developing tensor computation software packages, and each language offers a different way of processing tensor data. For example, TensorLy [2] and tntorch [3] are developed for Python, TensorToolbox [4], Tensorlab [5] are developed for MATLAB, while Uni10 [6] and SPLATT [7] are developed using C/C++. This means that readers can choose different programming languages based on the convenience of these software packages, which helps readers accomplish their seismic data processing tasks through their usage habits.

These tensor computation software packages have been developed to focus on different application domains and tasks. However, no dedicated software package exists to carry out tensor continuation for seismic data processing, which might be one of our future directions. Fortunately, most existing packages can perform the requested tensor operations and decompositions of the seismic data processing tasks discussed in this book. Moreover, these software packages offer readers numerous tensor decompositions not covered in this book, providing possibilities for future task extensions. For instance, tntorch [3] and hottbox [8] can handle tensor regression, classification, and statistical analysis problems. Notably, no single software package integrates all required tensor operations on one platform. For this reason, we will turn to different platforms to achieve their diverse goals and refer to the corresponding user manuals.Table A.1
The landscape of software package for tensor computation
Package name
Language
Package homepage
Description
TensorLy
Python
https://github.com/tensorly/tensorly
Designed to simplify tensor learning, offering straightforward tensor decomposition, learning, and algebra
tntorch
Python
https://tntorch.readthedocs.io/en/latest/
Facilitates tensor modeling and learning with seamless support for various frameworks, including the tensor train (TT) model, CANDECOMP/PARAFAC (CP), the Tucker model, and others
TensorD
Python
https://github.com/litpuvn/tensorD
Includes fundamental decomposition techniques like Tucker and CP decompositions, along with newer methods such as Pairwise Interaction Tensor Decomposition
Scikit-tensor
Python
https://github.com/mnick/scikit-tensor
Multilinear algebra and tensor factorizations, supporting basic operations such as folding/unfolding and tensor-matrix/vector products, as well as factorizations including CP, Tucker, RESCAL, DEDICOM, and INDSCAL
hottbox
Python
https://github.com/hottbox/hottbox
Offers a suite of tools for multi-dimensional operations, tensor decompositions, and sophisticated algorithms designed for multi-linear classification and data fusion. These include methods such as the Support Tensor Machine (STM) and Tensor Ensemble Learning (TEL)
TT toolbox
MATLAB and Python
https://github.com/oseledets/TT-Toolbox
Performing basic operations on high-dimensional tensors using the efficient Tensor Train (TT) format
Tensor toolbox
MATLAB
https://www.tensortoolbox.org/
Basic tensor operations and decompositions (such as CP and Tucker) for dense, sparse, and structured tensors
Tensorlab
MATLAB
https://www.tensorlab.net/
Supplies a variety of tools for tensor operations, (coupled) tensor factorizations, and advanced optimization
TTeMPS
MATLAB
https://www.epfl.ch/labs/anchp/index-html/software/ttemps/
Created for exploring algorithms in the Tensor Train (TT) and Matrix Product States (MPS) formats
TDALAB
MATLAB
https://github.com/andrewssobral/TDALAB
Delivers core data structures and methods for managing and processing tensor data
HT toolbox
MATLAB
https://www.epfl.ch/labs/anchp/index-html/software/htucker/
Facilitates efficient tensor storage and manipulation in hierarchical Tucker format, while also providing tools for developing advanced algorithms
n-way toolbox
MATLAB
https://github.com/andrewssobral/nway
Offers methods for fitting multi-way PARAFAC models, multi-way PLS regression models, and multi-way Tucker models
Uni10
C++
https://gitlab.com/uni10/uni10
Created for the advancement of tensor network algorithms
mptensor
C++
https://github.com/smorita/mptensor
Offers standard operations such as tensor contraction and t-SVD
iTensor
C++
https://itensor.org/
Designing and executing cutting-edge tensor network computations
cuTensor
C++
https://github.com/NVIDIA/CUDALibrarySamples
Fast implementation of operations related to t-SVD

C and OpenMP
https://github.com/ShadenSmith/splatt
Sparse tensor factorization: optimized and parallelized multiplication of sparse tensors and matrices
